hero_description: RVM: a runtime built around agents. A rotating four-dimensional wireframe, communication field and orange trajectory introduce capability-governed agent execution.
intro: Follow an agent through RVM: from machine entry and coherence domains to capability checks, memory, verified RVF packages, governed context, and recovery.
cta: [Build RVM](../userguide/01-quickstart.md) · [Explore the API and concepts](../userguide/) · [Read the design decisions](adr/) · [View releases](https://github.com/ruvnet/rvm/releases)

chapters.title: An agent-native stack
chapters.subtitle: A small core. Explicit boundaries. Optional extensions.
chapters.summary: Machine entry, the core, coherence, adapters, and persistent state.
chapters.body: RVM separates machine entry, its Rust `no_std` core, an optional coherence engine, execution adapters, and persistent state. Partitions are the units of isolation and scheduling. Capabilities carry authority; witnesses record privileged transitions. The coherence engine can be disabled without removing the core.
chapters.description: An agent-native stack. Machine entry, the core, coherence, adapters, and persistent state.

chapters.title: Bring the kernel online
chapters.subtitle: Initialize the foundations before handing off work.
chapters.summary: The seven phases in the kernel initialization sequence.
chapters.body: The ADR-137 boot sequence advances through reset, hardware detection, MMU setup, hypervisor mode, kernel object initialization, the first witness, and scheduler entry. Each completed phase records a witness before advancing. The diagram follows the current BootStage implementation and is an architectural walkthrough, not a captured boot session.
chapters.description: Bring the kernel online. The seven phases in the kernel initialization sequence.

chapters.title: Let the graph shape isolation
chapters.subtitle: Communication and cut pressure inform placement.
chapters.summary: Agent communication feeds the optional coherence control loop.
chapters.body: Communication edges form a weighted graph. The optional coherence engine tracks locality and cut pressure, and supports partition restructuring through split, merge, and migration. Animated node clusters illustrate changing relationships; no latency or optimality guarantee is implied by the motion.
chapters.description: Let the graph shape isolation. Agent communication feeds the optional coherence control loop.

chapters.title: Authority before mutation
chapters.subtitle: Capability checks, proof verification, and a witness.
chapters.footer: A REFUSED REQUEST DOES NOT MUTATE STATE
chapters.summary: A request passes the security gate before its state transition.
chapters.body: RVM checks capability authority and verifies the required proof before a permitted state transition. Its security path emits witness records for decisions, including refusals. Proof requirements vary by operation and tier; this diagram does not imply that every path uses a zero-knowledge proof.
chapters.description: Authority before mutation. A request passes the security gate before its state transition.

chapters.title: Schedule with two signals
chapters.subtitle: Deadline urgency meets isolation pressure.
chapters.summary: The scheduler combines time urgency with graph-derived pressure.
chapters.body: RVM scheduling uses deadline urgency and cut pressure. The first represents time-sensitive work; the second represents pressure from the coherence graph. This view explains the two inputs without prescribing weights. Animation speed is illustrative.
chapters.description: Schedule with two signals. The scheduler combines time urgency with graph-derived pressure.

chapters.title: Keep state at the right tier
chapters.subtitle: Hot, warm, dormant, and cold memory.
chapters.summary: Memory tiers, checkpoints, and witness-based reconstruction.
chapters.body: Memory regions have ownership and a tier: Hot, Warm, Dormant, or Cold. Dormant state can combine a checkpoint with a compressed witness trail for reconstruction. Tier transitions and recovery depend on the configured runtime and storage path; the drawing is a conceptual lifecycle.
chapters.description: Keep state at the right tier. Memory tiers, checkpoints, and witness-based reconstruction.

chapters.title: Choose an execution boundary
chapters.subtitle: Hosted isolation and bare-metal targets are distinct.
chapters.summary: A verified workload uses the isolation its selected adapter supports.
chapters.body: The hosted path uses `rvm-host` to select available OS isolation and launch supported workloads, including WASM. Bare-metal partitions use the kernel target and its hardware mechanisms. Hosted WASM or an OS sandbox must not be described as bare-metal partition isolation. Optional GPU access is separately feature- and capability-gated.
chapters.description: Choose an execution boundary. A verified workload uses the isolation its selected adapter supports.

chapters.title: Verify, then execute
chapters.subtitle: RVForge packages meet the RVM execution contract.
chapters.summary: RVForge authors packages; RVM verifies, maps, places, and launches them.
chapters.body: RVForge authors and signs an RVF. `rvm-rvf` verifies its manifest and segments, maps capability requirements, and preserves package identity. `rvm-host` selects isolation and placement; `rvm-launch` manages the instance lifecycle. Inspect and verify do not execute the package. Unsupported capability requests are refused and witnessed.
chapters.description: Verify, then execute. RVForge authors packages; RVM verifies, maps, places, and launches them.

chapters.title: Reconstruct the evidence
chapters.subtitle: Append-only records connect state transitions.
chapters.summary: A witness chain connects privileged operations and recovery checkpoints.
chapters.body: Witness records form an append-only, hash-chained audit trail. Checkpoint and replay mechanisms support recovery and forensic reconstruction of recorded transitions. The trace is illustrative: it contains no real workload, secrets, timestamps, or fabricated test results.
chapters.description: Reconstruct the evidence. A witness chain connects privileged operations and recovery checkpoints.

chapters.title: A name is not permission
chapters.subtitle: Resolve governed ruv:// context only after authorization.
chapters.summary: An out-of-band capability governs access to immutable context revisions.
chapters.body: A `ruv://` URI is an inert name. Live capabilities arrive out of band; authorization and witnessing precede resolution or retrieval. RVF revisions are immutable, aliases update through compare-and-swap, and reads carry epoch receipts. Reading a skill does not execute it: execution requires a pinned URI and a separate permit.
chapters.description: A name is not permission. An out-of-band capability governs access to immutable context revisions.

chapters.title: Anchor external evidence
chapters.subtitle: Verify a receipt before committing its anchor.
chapters.summary: External evaluation receipt commitments can enter the RVM witness chain.
chapters.body: `rvm-anchor` verifies external evaluation receipts and anchors their commitments into the witness chain. An anchor preserves a verifiable relationship to supplied evidence; it does not independently prove that an external evaluator or its conclusion is correct.
chapters.description: Anchor external evidence. External evaluation receipt commitments can enter the RVM witness chain.

chapters.title: Build your first RVM
chapters.subtitle: Start with the workspace, then choose a target.
chapters.footer: OPEN THE QUICK START FOR TARGET PREREQUISITES
chapters.summary: Check and test the Rust workspace, then follow the platform build guide.
chapters.body: Clone with submodules because RVM consumes RuVector components. Run the host workspace checks first. The quick-start guide lists the AArch64 toolchain, QEMU, and binary conversion tools needed for the bare-metal build and run steps.
chapters.description: Build your first RVM. Check and test the Rust workspace, then follow the platform build guide.
chapters.command:
git clone --recurse-submodules https://github.com/ruvnet/rvm.git
cd rvm
cargo check
cargo test --workspace --lib
